newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi's parliament speaker leaves embassy.
newsitem.headline: Burundi's parliament speaker leaves embassy.

text.p: The speaker of Burundi's parliament left the German ambassador's residence on Wednesday, more than two months after he sought refuge there during a military takeover.
German embassy sources said Leonce Ngendakumana, an ethnic Hutu, left at 10.30 a.m. (0830 GMT), and was driven to the speaker's official residence by German ambassador Bernd Morast.
Ngendakumana was one of 18 prominent Hutus who took asylum in the German embassy in the tense hours before the mainly-Tutsi army seized power last July 25.
The speaker was the last to leave and his decision followed security guarantees given by the military government under Major Pierre Buyoya, sources in Ngendukamana's Frodebu party said.
His departure meant that ex-president Sylvestre Ntibantunganya is the last senior Hutu politician under diplomatic protection.

Ntibantunganya has been at the U.S. ambassador's residence since July 23. Buyoya's spokesman says he is allowed to leave Burundi but must first go to his personal residence and must not leave directly from the U.S. embassy.

The national assembly (parliament) was restored by Buyoya last month as part of moves aimed at lifting regional sanctions against Burundi. The 81-seat assembly is supposed to meet on October 7 but more than half the 65 Frodebu members are in exile, saying their security is in danger at home.
